title_en: The Section on the Unfathomable One
translit:
|| Ath shri Agadhaka Ang ||5||

Kabir aadya ant Hari ek hai | kahan sunankun doy ||
Pala the jal hot hai | jal the pala hoy ||1||
Aad ant sab ek hai | madhya maya vistar ||
Naam sharan jan Jivana | gun mein sab sansar ||2||
Jaise ka taisa Hari | aadi ant sab ek ||
Bhagat manorath Jivana | Hari dharyo gopko bhes ||3||
Nirakar aakar the | adbhut ek arup ||
So Sain hamare Jivana | je Sitapatiko rup ||4||
Nirakar nirdhar hai | aakare anand ||
God khelave Jashomati | so puran premanand ||5||
E rup arupe Shamalo | khele Nand dvar ||
Aadi Omkar upanyo | koti brahmand vistar ||6||
Omkar pahelo Jivana | sundar Shyam swarup ||
So Gokul manhe govaliyo | je Dasharath-kul badbhup ||7||
Nabhi kamal Brahma hava | so Gokul manhi goval ||
Aadi Omkar upanyo Jivana | je koti brahmand vistar ||8||
Nabhi kamal Brahma hava | so Gokul manhi goval ||
Mor pichchh shir ghunghchi | so Jivan Vraj pratipal ||9||
Aakar kahu to ang nahi | ang bin kaiso updesh ||
Var par nahi Jivana | Hari dharyo Natvar vesh ||10||
Nirgun sargun Jivana | so Brijkul chare gay ||
Sargun Vrishabhanki davdi | nirgun Jadupati Ray ||11||
Ashadh unamyo Jivana | aiso Shyam swarup ||
Bhitar chamke damini | so Radhajiko rup ||12||
Vrindavanki kunjmen | khelat gopi goval ||
So pran jivan mere Jivana | je Vrishabhansuta Nandlal ||13||
Ladu payo Radhika | ang bhari chumban det ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | so sab sakhiyanke het ||14||
Bhakti bharvadan bhavti | rachi pachi ho gaye ek ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | apne man vivek ||15||
Shesh sukhasan Jivana | Lakshmi charan nivas ||
Nabhi kamal Brahma hava | so Nand ghar pive chhas ||16||
Kaun bhakti bharvad ki | paye rab aur chhas ||
Gau charave Jivana | bohotek kari uphas ||17||
Has vinode Hari mile | munijan rahe udas ||
Dhanya prit bharvadki Jivana | paye rab aur chhas ||18||
Krishnavatare kamini | Raghupati kino jog ||
Ved vachan kahe Jivana | nari lino bhog ||19||
Pativrata pichhe padi | je gopiye kiyo vyabhichar ||
Has vinode Jivana | milyo purvalo bharthar ||20||
Ladu badhu Nandko | trividh tap mit jay ||
Koi ek gurumukh Jivana | je Hari ras piye aghay ||21||
Ladu badho Nandko | Vasudev dino jay ||
Kodi badle Jivana | ratan diyo dharkay ||22||
Uchhino udhar kiyo | Jashomati ke Devaki ||
Bhur jat bharvad ki | pan samo lino olakhi ||23||
Penda Parbrahm namka | tin lok shir taj ||
Gokul govalo pragatyo Jivana | jine kiyo Ayodhya raj ||24||
Dashe avatare Shamalo | chovise akhand ||
Sab sakhiyanman Jivana | vyapo koti brahmand ||25||
Harie gau charavi Nandki | sab sakhiyanke updesh ||
Prem badhayo Jivana | na jane Shankar Shesh ||26||
Harie gau chari Nandki | sab sakhiyanke updesh ||
Varpar nahi Jivana | Harie dharyo gopko bhesh ||27||
Main dadhi mahi sate Jivana | payo Jadupati Ray ||
Sharir sompu aapano | to lila kaise thay ||28||
So Sain hamare Jivana | jakun Shankar dhay ||
So kali aay pragate | je Gokul chari gay ||29||
Sajan hamare Ramji | je Vrishabhan sutako dhyan ||
Taku dhyavat Jivana | so sajan praman ||30||
Kaustubh mani mukh morli | sundar Shyam sharir ||
Rup rekh vapu nahi Jivana | aise he Raghuvir ||31||
Nayan saluno Shamalo | Radhajiko dhyan ||
Jan Jivanko hirde baso | je Sagarsutako dhyan ||32||
Vaikunth chhandi Jivana | takyo Gokul gam ||
Sol kalasu Shamalo | sakal sevak sukh dham ||33||
Chhappan bhog puran bhaye | payo dudh aur bhat ||
Krishnavatare Jivana | aroge Raghunath ||34||
Purush nakaro jo kare | to nar tede tahan jay ||
Rishipatnipe Jivana | Jadupati bhaye sahay ||35||
Rishipatnipe pahuna | Hari bhaye Jivandas ||
Man vanchhit phal purke | puri abala aash ||36||
Mohe niki lagat Jivana | je gali det goval ||
Char ved Brahma padhe | so mere man kal ||37||
Bharuade bhale bholavyo | chaud bhuvanno Nath ||
Ranchi ek makhan karane | daman bandho hath ||38||
Damodar daman bandhiyo | makhan karan mat ||
Yamala-Arjun karane Jivana | koi na jane ghat ||39||
Damodar daman bandhiyo | jene kahyo je chhod ||
Bandhan take Jivana | kate chorasi kod ||40||
Bhagya bado te Jivana | je Mathura liyo avatar ||
Kaha pankhi kaha manavi | kaha gopi gay goval ||41||
Vrindavanman Jivana | sab pankhi karat kalol ||
Nandghar dulaho pragatyo | ham nirkhat jugal kishor ||42||
Nandghar dulaho pragatyo | mudit bhai sab gay ||
Sham sakha sang Jivana | mukh chumbat kanth lagay ||43||
Bhakti het bharvadki | Gokul charai gay ||
Kansasur maryo Jivana | Ugrasen diyo chhoday ||44||
Kot brahmandpati Kahanavo | so aayo Gokul manhi ||
Ven vajade Jivana | shri Bansibatki chhanhi ||45||
Ayodhyathi aaviyo | Gokul charavi gay ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | hath ghase kahe hay ||46||
Bhakti het bharvadki | pragate puran Brahm ||
Bhakt manorath Jivana | Hari kiyo ahirko karm ||47||
Mohane jag mohiya | Hari Vrajke pran ||
Vrindavanman Jivana | mare morliyan ban ||48||
Kachhuk kangaiman kaman kiyo | shish gunthat Brijnar ||
Tabthe Jadupati Jivana | dole ghar ghar dvar ||49||
Garud vahan Gopal taj | nagan panahi nahi pay ||
Bhakt manorath Jivana | Hari Gokul charai gay ||50||
Ratnakarki putri | aavi Vrikhbhanke dvar ||
Raghupati chhandi Jivana | so Shyame diyo vihar ||51||
Vrindavanman Shamalo | dadhi khay sab lut ||
Brahma chhal kiyo Jivana | navi jugati anup ||52||
Vrindavanman Shamalo | mukh morli ghanghor ||
Sab sakhiyanman Jivana | jay jay Jugalkishor ||53||
Nirgun sirgun Jivana | doy hamare Ram ||
Ved dharmman Raghupati | nirgun gopiko dham ||54||
Nand gharuni Jivana | hasi hasi chumban det ||
Nirgun the sirgun bhayo | so sab sakhiyanke het ||55||
Kar kamal lai Jivana | Kali nathyo Kahan ||
Brij mandal pavan kiyo | ahipati maradyo man ||56||
Jot swarupi vede kahyo | sakal bhakt pratipal ||
Brahmadik bhule Jivana | so khele bal Gopal ||57||
Vrindavanman Jivana | Shame bajavyo bansh ||
Bhakt het avatar liyo | pragate Mansarovar hans ||58||
Vrindavanman Jivana | dise kshir samudra ||
Sab sakhiyanman Radhika | jyun udghanman chandra ||59||
Vrindavanman Jivana | jit dekhun tit lal ||
So lali Hari namki | Radha lal gulal ||60||
Eh lila tab bhai Jivana | Vrikhbhansutake sang ||
Lalisun lali mali | tab nikaso rang sorang ||61||
Shesh Mahesh sab Jivana | Ved na pave par ||
Tathe sabthe chup bhali | gaiye Nandkumar ||62||
Shesh Maheshwar Jivana | nish din mokun dhay ||
Je ras pino gvalani | so bund na chakhan pay ||63||
Charan parsat taruni dhasi | kiya Kalindi su vichar ||
Huan kahet he Jivana | nishdin Vrajki lahar ||64||
translation:
Here begins the Ang (section) of Agadh, the Unfathomable One — the fifth. (Kabir's sakhis, couplets, addressed throughout to "Jivana" — the disciple Jivanji.)

1. Kabir says: at the beginning and at the end Hari is one; only in the telling and the hearing does He seem to be two. Out of ice water comes to be, and out of water ice comes to be.

2. Beginning and end are all one; only in the middle is the spread of maya (illusion). O Jivan, the servant takes refuge in the Name, while the whole world is caught up in the gunas (the qualities of nature).

3. Hari is exactly as He always was; beginning and end, all one. O Jivan, to fulfil the devotee's longing Hari put on the guise of a cowherd.

4. The formless took on form — wondrous, one, and without shape. O Jivan, that is our Lord (Sain), who is the very form of Sita's husband.

5. Formless, He is without any support; in form, He is bliss itself. Jashomati (Yashoda) dandles Him in her lap — that is perfect love-bliss.

6. This form of the formless, the dark one (Shyam), plays at Nanda's door. From Him the primal Omkar arose, and the spreading out of ten million universes.

7. O Jivan, before Omkar there was that beautiful dark form. He is the cowherd boy in Gokul, and He is the great king of Dasharath's line.

8. From the lotus of His navel Brahma came to be — and He is the cowherd in Gokul. O Jivan, from Him arose the primal Omkar and the spreading out of ten million universes.

9. From the lotus of His navel Brahma came to be — and He is the cowherd in Gokul. With a peacock plume and gunja berries on His head, O Jivan, He is the sustainer of Vraj.

10. If I call Him form, He has no limbs; and without limbs, what teaching could He give? He has no near shore and no far shore, O Jivan — and yet Hari put on the dress of Natvar, the divine dancer.

11. Nirgun (without qualities) and sargun (with qualities), O Jivan — He grazes the cows of the house of Vraj. The sargun is Vrishabhan's daughter; the nirgun is Jadupati, the king.

12. O Jivan, like the clouds rising in Ashadh (the monsoon month) is Shyam's dark form; the lightning that flashes within it is Radhaji's form.

13. In the bowers of Vrindavan the gopis and cowherds are at play. O Jivan, they are the very life-breath of me — Vrishabhan's daughter and Nanda's darling son.

14. Radhika has won the darling boy; she holds Him close and covers Him with kisses. O Jivan, Brahma and the gods are left bewildered — all of this is for the love of the sakhis (companions).

15. The bhakti (devotion) of the herdsmen is dear to Him; steeped and soaked in it, they became one with Him. O Jivan, Brahma and the rest forgot themselves — forgot their own pride and their discernment.

16. O Jivan, Shesha is His couch of ease, Lakshmi dwells at His feet, from His navel-lotus Brahma came to be — and He drinks buttermilk in Nanda's house.

17. What sort of devotion is this of the herdsmen, that He takes their gruel and their buttermilk? O Jivan, He grazes the cows and puts up with a great deal of mockery.

18. Through laughter and playfulness Hari is found, while the sages remain aloof and joyless. Blessed is the love of the herdsmen, O Jivan — for it He accepted their gruel and buttermilk.

19. In the Krishna avatar there were the loving women; as Raghupati (Ram) He held to yoga. O Jivan, the word of the Veda says it: in that form He took the enjoyment of woman.

20. The chaste wives were left behind, while the gopis were charged with adultery. Yet through laughter and playfulness, O Jivan, they found again the husband who had been theirs in a former birth.

21. Nanda's darling boy grows, and by Him the threefold suffering is wiped away. Only some rare gurumukh (one whose face is turned to the guru), O Jivan, drinks the nectar of Hari to his fill.

22. The darling boy grew up as Nanda's; Vasudeva went and gave Him away. O Jivan, in exchange for a cowrie shell he let a jewel slip from his hands.

23. Was it a loan given or a loan taken — by Jashomati or by Devaki? The herdsmen's caste is simple and unlettered, and yet she recognized Him for what He was.

24. The path is the Name of Parbrahm (the Supreme), the crown upon the head of the three worlds. O Jivan, He appeared as a cowherd in Gokul — He who once ruled the kingdom of Ayodhya.

25. In all ten avatars it is the same dark Lord; through all twenty-four He is unbroken. O Jivan, He is present among all the sakhis and pervades ten million universes.

26. Hari grazed Nanda's cows — and that itself was His teaching to all the sakhis. O Jivan, He made such love grow as even Shankar and Shesha do not know.

27. Hari grazed Nanda's cows — His teaching to all the sakhis. He has neither this shore nor that, O Jivan, and yet Hari put on the guise of a cowherd.

28. O Jivan, in exchange for curds and buttermilk I obtained Jadupati, the king. If I hand over this body of mine to Him, then how would His lila (divine play) go on?

29. O Jivan, that is our Lord, the one toward whom even Shankar runs. He has come and shown Himself in the Kali age — He who grazed the cows in Gokul.

30. Our beloved is Ramji, on whom Vrishabhan's daughter meditates. O Jivan, whoever meditates on Him — that one is a true and worthy person.

31. The Kaustubh jewel, the flute at His lips, the beautiful dark body — and yet He has no form, no outline, no body at all, O Jivan: such is Raghuvir.

32. The dark one with the lovely eyes is Radhaji's meditation. May He dwell in the heart of His servant Jivan — He on whom the ocean's daughter meditates.

33. O Jivan, He left Vaikunth and chose the village of Gokul instead. Complete with all sixteen kalas (portions of perfection), the dark Lord is the abode of joy for all His servants.

34. The fifty-six offerings were fulfilled when He was given milk and rice. O Jivan, in the Krishna avatar it is Raghunath Himself who eats.

35. When the husbands refused, the wives went where they were being called. O Jivan, Jadupati became the helper of the sages' wives.

36. Hari became the guest of the sages' wives, O Jivandas. Granting the fruit their hearts desired, He fulfilled the hope of those helpless women.

37. O Jivan, sweet to me are even the abuses the cowherds fling at Him. The four Vedas that Brahma recites — to my mind those are death.

38. How well the herd-woman coaxed the Lord of the fourteen worlds! For the sake of one scrap of butter His hands were tied with a rope.

39. Damodar was bound with a rope by His mother, on account of the butter. O Jivan, it was really for the sake of the Yamala-Arjuna trees — no one knew what He was about.

40. Damodar was bound with a rope; and whoever said "let Him go" — O Jivan, for that one the bondage of the eighty-four lakh births is cut away.

41. Great is their good fortune, O Jivan, that He took birth at Mathura — whether they be birds or human beings, gopis or cows or cowherds.

42. O Jivan, in Vrindavan all the birds are singing for joy. In Nanda's house the bridegroom has appeared, and we gaze upon the youthful pair.

43. In Nanda's house the bridegroom has appeared, and all the cows are glad. O Jivan, Shyam is among His companions, kissing their faces and clasping them to His breast.

44. For the sake of the herdsmen's devotion He grazed the cows in Gokul. O Jivan, He killed the demon Kamsa and set Ugrasena free.

45. Kanha, the lord of ten million universes, came into Gokul. O Jivan, He plays His flute in the shade of the holy Bansi-vat (the banyan of the flute).

46. He came from Ayodhya and grazed the cows in Gokul. O Jivan, Brahma and the gods missed it, and now they wring their hands and cry "alas!"

47. For the sake of the herdsmen's devotion the perfect Brahman appeared. O Jivan, to fulfil His devotees' longing Hari did the work of a cowherd.

48. The enchanter has enchanted the world; Hari is the life-breath of Vraj. O Jivan, in Vrindavan He shoots the arrows of His flute.

49. The women of Vraj worked some spell into the comb as they dressed His hair. O Jivan, ever since then Jadupati wanders from house to house, from door to door.

50. Gopal gave up Garuda His mount; bare, without even sandals on His feet. O Jivan, to fulfil His devotees' longing Hari grazed the cows in Gokul.

51. The daughter of the ocean came to Vrishabhan's door. O Jivan, she whom Raghupati had left behind was given the joy of His play by Shyam.

52. In Vrindavan the dark one eats the curds and plunders them all. O Jivan, Brahma played his trick on Him, and He answered with a new and matchless device.

53. In Vrindavan the dark one holds the flute to His lips, sounding deep as thunder. O Jivan, among all the sakhis — victory, victory to the youthful pair!

54. Nirgun and sargun both, O Jivan, are our Ram. In the dharma of the Vedas He is Raghupati; the nirgun is the gopis' own dwelling.

55. O Jivan, Nanda's wife laughs and laughs and kisses Him. The nirgun became the sargun — and all of it for the love of the sakhis.

56. With His lotus hands, O Jivan, Kanha subdued Kaliya. He made the whole circle of Vraj pure and crushed the pride of the serpent king.

57. The Vedas called Him the very form of light, the sustainer of all devotees. O Jivan, Brahma and the gods were left bewildered — and He plays about as the child Gopal.

58. O Jivan, in Vrindavan Shyam played upon His flute. For His devotees' sake He took birth — the swan of Mansarovar has appeared.

59. O Jivan, Vrindavan looks like the ocean of milk; and among all the sakhis Radhika shines as the moon does amid the drifting clouds.

60. O Jivan, in Vrindavan wherever I look, there is the Beloved. That redness is the redness of Hari's Name — Radha and the Beloved, red with gulal (coloured powder).

61. This lila came about, O Jivan, in the company of Vrishabhan's daughter. Redness met with redness, and then a colour of pure splendour came forth.

62. Shesha, Mahesh and all the rest, O Jivan — not even the Vedas reach His far shore. So silence is better than all speech: let us simply sing of Nanda's son.

63. O Jivan, Shesha and Maheshwar hasten toward me night and day; yet the nectar the cowherd women drank — of that they do not get to taste a single drop.

64. Touching His feet the young woman plunged in, and took counsel with the Kalindi (the Yamuna). There, they say, O Jivan, the waves of Vraj rise night and day.
